newsitem.title: USA: Dollar ends near day's highs in U.S. vs mark, yen.
newsitem.headline: Dollar ends near day's highs in U.S. vs mark, yen.

text.p: The dollar rose to a 33-month high against the Japanese yen and a 20-week high against the German mark on the continued strength of the British pound and a spike in oil prices, foreign exchange dealers said.
Sterling posted new highs for the third consecutive session as investors jumped in to capitalize on the rally.

"Right now, a lot of people have to buy sterling. They are getting caught at these levels; surprised at how fast it's moved up," said Mark Gargano, managing director of currency derivatives at First Union National Bank.

The pound touched a one-year high of 1.5893 against the dollar and a 44-month high of 178.05 against the yen in late U.S. trade. Sterling closed at $1.5876/81. A rise in sterling tends to aid the dollar as investment flows out of other currencies in Japan and Europe, dealers said.
"The start of this whole move in the dollar was the rise in sterling/mark," said Seth Garrett, chief dealer at CS First Boston.
Meanwhile, a spike to six-year highs in oil prices, coupled with increased expectations that Japan will hold steady domestic interest rates hurt the yen.

Japanese polls show the ruling Liberal Democratic Party will likely lead the next government coalition after the October 20th general election, keeping in place its present policy of delaying an increase in Japanese interest rates.
Also, Japan relies heavily on imported oil and therefore is especially vulnerable to a rise in oil prices.

The dollar touched a high of 112.39 yen in early U.S. trade, up from Tuesday's open of 112.24/34. The dollar ended little changed at 112.26/31 yen. The dollar closed at 1.5405/15 marks after touching a 1.5412 mark high. The dollar opened on Tuesday at 1.5393/98 marks.
Dealers also cited pent-up demand for dollars after the U.S. currency spent the last several sessions in a very narrow trading range.
The dollar finally broke through stubborn technical resistance on Tuesday, attracting considerable buying interest, dealers said.
"When we took out some key levels on the way up today, we fueled a rally," Garrett said.
U.S. stocks and bonds ended little changed on Tuesday, but the recent strength of U.S. assets continues to bolster the dollar, dealers said.
"There is still a lot of capital flowing into those markets and as long as there are no major set-backs, they will continue to help the dollar," Gargano said.
Finland's entry over the weekend into the European Exchange Rate Mechanism weighed heavily for a second day on the currencies of leading European nations, dealers said.
"I think that is really what's pulling the dollar up against Europe," said Bill Bertha, chief dealer at Mellon Bank.
Dealers said they are focused on Wednesday's scheduled release of the U.S. September consumer price index.

A stronger-than-expected number could harm the dollar, dealers said. A Reuter poll shows a consensus Wall Street forecast for a 0.3 percent rise in September CPI compared with a 0.1 percent gain in August.
In other trade, the dollar closed at 1.2685/95 Swiss francs, up from 1.2662/72 at Tuesday's open. The greenback ended at Canadian $1.3543/48 after opening at C$1.3522/37.
The Australian dollar closed off at $0.7895/00 after opening at $0.7910/15. -- Roanne Daniels, 212-859-1677
